advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Extend test_spies_actually_fire_on_a_leaky_stub to invoke every patched seam (batch_write_and_push, batch_stage_and_commit, delete_events, subprocess.check_output/check_call, socket.socket.connect_ex) so all 12 spies are proven load-bearing.
evidence: Self-check only calls: subprocess.run, subprocess.Popen, time.sleep, event_append.write_and_push, event_append.stage_and_commit, socket.socket.connect (lines 119-134)

The file's own docstring frames the self-check as the guard that lets 'an ABSENCE of EffectViolation' be trusted 'rather than "the spy was never wired at all"' -- but that guarantee only holds for the 6 seams it actually exercises.
advisory.finding: The effect-spy self-check test only proves 6 of the 12 patched effect seams are load-bearing tripwires; subprocess.check_output/check_call, socket.socket.connect_ex, event_append.batch_write_and_push/batch_stage_and_commit/delete_events are patched but never self-checked, so the corpus-replay tests' ABSENCE of EffectViolation for those six cannot be distinguished from a spy that was never a real tripwire.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add match-corpus scenarios whose legacy payloads OMIT optional keys (outbound create with no comments/labels, outbound update with only changed_fields, inbound update without local_id) to exercise the as_legacy_dict round-trip asymmetry, or make the projections omit keys the source lacked.
evidence: OutboundCreatePayload.as_legacy_dict always sets out['comments'] and out['labels'] (mutation_payloads.py as_legacy_dict body)

test_outbound_create_open_ended_fields_allow_arbitrary_keys asserts input {'any_vendor_field': 1} projects to {'any_vendor_field': 1, 'comments': [], 'labels': []} -- confirming keys are ADDED, not preserved

Corpus outbound_create/outbound_update/inbound_update match scenarios all include comments/labels/links/changed_fields keys (scenarios.json lines 8-16, 44-49, 179-194), so no match scenario exercises a payload that omits an optional key
ADR 0107 comment records that differ.py emits flat/subset outbound-update and inbound-create shapes that DO omit these wrapper keys -- exactly the shapes that would diverge.
advisory.finding: Several as_legacy_dict() projections unconditionally emit optional collection keys (OutboundCreatePayload always emits comments/labels; OutboundUpdatePayload always emits changed_fields+comments+labels+links; InboundUpdatePayload always emits local_id/fields/labels/comments/links), so a legacy dict payload that omits any of those keys would round-trip to a payload with the key added, breaking the byte-identity the shadow comparator asserts -- an asymmetry the v1 corpus never surfaces because every match scenario already supplies those keys.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Assert the replayed corpus is non-empty (e.g. `assert match_scenarios` and `assert reject_scenarios`, or `assert results`) in test_full_corpus_replay_never_trips_an_effect_spy so the no-effect verdict cannot pass vacuously.
evidence: assert all(r.matched for r in results.values())
ABSENCE: no `assert match_scenarios` / `assert results` / non-empty-count check anchors the corpus as non-empty before the absence-of-EffectViolation verdict is trusted
advisory.finding: The AC2 safety-oracle test `test_full_corpus_replay_never_trips_an_effect_spy` passes vacuously if the loaded corpus contains no match/reject scenarios: `assert all(r.matched for r in results.values())` is vacuously true over an empty dict and the `for scenario in reject_scenarios` loop is a no-op, so a corpus that was emptied, mis-filtered, or failed to populate would report 'no effect tripped' without ever driving the shadow path under the armed spies. No liveness anchor (e.g. `assert results` / `assert match_scenarios and reject_scenarios`) establishes the producer actually ran.
scenarios: Corpus file emptied or scenario schema changes so expect-filter yields [] — the effect-spy replay test stays green while exercising nothing
advisory.suggested_fix: Add `assert match_scenarios, "corpus has no match scenarios"` and `assert reject_scenarios, "corpus has no reject scenarios"` before the loops, plus `assert results` after compare_corpus.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Consider strengthening the route-census guard to an import-graph/AST check (or asserting the modules' resolved imports) rather than a substring grep over a fixed module list.
evidence: _PRODUCTION_MODULES = ( typed_dispatch, batch_dispatch, apply_base, differ, outbound_mutation_builders, run_differs, outbound_pass, binding_walk, invariants, )
advisory.finding: `test_no_production_dispatch_module_imports_the_shadow_modules` enforces the AC7 unwired boundary via a raw source-text substring grep (`new_name not in source`) over a hard-coded list of 9 production modules. It is a change-detector (renaming either new module silently makes the guard pass) and only covers the enumerated modules, so a NEW production module wiring the shadow path would not be caught; a mention of the module name in a comment could also false-fail.
scenarios: A future/other production module wires build_typed_payload but is not in _PRODUCTION_MODULES — census passes despite the coupling
